演奏玻璃馬林巴琴時，先將玻璃鍵置於節點支撐上，再以琴槌敲擊鍵面發聲。初學可先用壓: To play the glass marimba, first rest the glass bars on supports at their nodes, then strike the bar with a mallet to sound it. A beginner can start with mallets of compressed silicone balls on wooden or synthetic shafts, striking and listening to the pure tone; if another effect is wanted, change to another mallet. The bars may be resonated by a single open box or by individual resonators, and the instrument sounds according to the arrangement used.

玻璃馬林巴琴以玻璃鍵取代木製鍵，屬體鳴樂器；鍵經單一開口共鳴箱或個別共鳴器放大。: The glass marimba replaces wooden bars with glass bars and is an idiophone; the bars are amplified by a single open resonator box or by individual resonators. Silicone ball mallets draw out the purest tone, and other heads give other effects. The range depends on the tuning system, and the thickness of the bars can be matched to different tunings; grinding the end of a bar raises the pitch, and if the glass is opaque, grinding the underside lowers it. The source does not clearly record how the volume is controlled, but the material of the mallet and the resonating structure both affect the sound. Beside the wooden marimba, its timbre is determined mainly by the glass bars, the way they are resonated and the mallets.

玻璃馬林巴琴屬體鳴樂器，以玻璃取代木製結構；以玻璃製成的樂器被稱為水晶樂器。其名: The glass marimba is an idiophone that replaces wooden parts with glass; instruments made of glass are called crystal instruments. Its name comes from an African language, possibly Bantu, and means “an instrument like the xylophone”. In its development the way of resonating decides the construction and design, either a single open box shared by all the bars or an individual resonator for each bar; the bars may be of flat glass or of stained glass, the latter often needing two pieces fused in a kiln to reach the needed thickness. The tuning system can be set as required, and the Brazilian percussion ensemble also uses the instrument.
玻璃馬林巴琴是一種以玻璃構件取代木製構件的體鳴樂器，屬玻璃樂器一類；「馬林巴」一: The glass marimba is an idiophone that replaces wooden parts with parts of glass, and belongs to the glass instruments; the word “marimba” comes from an African language and means an instrument like the xylophone. Its bars are of flat glass or stained glass, and it can be resonated by a single open box or by individual resonators, and struck with silicone ball mallets. The tuning system can be set as required. The Brazilian percussion ensemble Uakti uses the instrument.
玻璃馬林巴琴的發聲體以玻璃取代木條，琴鍵可用平板玻璃或彩繪玻璃；彩繪玻璃需兩片窯: On the glass marimba the sounding body replaces wooden bars with glass, and the bars may be of flat glass or stained glass; stained glass needs two pieces fired together to about a quarter of an inch thick, and thinner or thicker glass suits different registers. The resonator box may be of wood, glass or metal, and individual resonators of gourd, wood, bamboo, clay, glass, PVC or metal. Where the bars are supported, perforated foam is laid over a thin wooden strip covered with cloth and fixed with double-sided clear tape, silicone, posts, Velcro or felt strips. The mallets may be wooden or synthetic shafts with compressed silicone balls stuck on.
